definitions.explanation: Sake brewed using only rice, water, rice koji, and yeast, with no added distilled alcohol.

examples.japanese: この{純米酒|じゅんまいしゅ}はおいしい。
{純米酒|じゅんまいしゅ}は{米|こめ}の{味|あじ}がしっかり{感|かん}じられる。
examples.english: With junmai sake, you can really taste the rice.

examples.japanese: {地元|じもと}の{酒蔵|さかぐら}で{造|つく}られた{純米酒|じゅんまいしゅ}を{土産|みやげ}に{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought a junmai sake made at a local brewery as a souvenir.

notes:
A compound of {純米|じゅんまい} (pure rice) and {酒|しゅ} (sake/alcohol). Junmai sake is distinguished from other sake categories by the absence of added {醸造|じょうぞう}アルコール (distilled alcohol). This gives it a fuller, richer body with more pronounced rice flavor.

SAKE CLASSIFICATION HIERARCHY:
- {純米酒|じゅんまいしゅ}: pure rice sake (no polishing ratio requirement)
- {純米吟醸酒|じゅんまいぎんじょうしゅ}: pure rice ginjo (rice polished to 60% or less)
- {純米大吟醸酒|じゅんまいだいぎんじょうしゅ}: pure rice daiginjo (rice polished to 50% or less)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {辛口|からくち}の{純米酒|じゅんまいしゅ}: dry junmai sake
- {甘口|あまくち}の{純米酒|じゅんまいしゅ}: sweet junmai sake
- {冷|ひ}やで{飲|の}む: to drink chilled
- {燗|かん}をつける: to warm (sake)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Junmai sake can be enjoyed at a wide range of temperatures, from chilled to warmed. Its robust flavor makes it especially popular for pairing with food.
